newsitem.title: MALI: Mali's Konare has massive lead in boycotted poll.
newsitem.headline: Mali's Konare has massive lead in boycotted poll.

text.p: Mali President Alpha Oumar Konare has opened a massive lead against his sole challenger in presidential elections boycotted by mainstream opposition parties, partial results showed on Tuesday.

Results released by the electoral commission gave Konare 85.15 percent of votes from Sunday's poll against 4.09 percent for businessman Mamadou Maribatrou Diaby in the second multi-party elections since independence in 1960.
The results, from six of the impoverished West African nation's eight regions, showed a turnout of just 27 percent.
The opposition, which had demanded that this year's national elections be postponed and reorganised after a chaotic April 13 parliamentary election, has said it will not respect the results.

"If transparent elections are not organised between now and June 8 there will be no president in the Republic of Mali," Mountaga Tall of the opposition National Democratic Initiative Congress told reporters.
"Alpha elected with 85 percent is a defeat and a shame," said the opposition Tambour newspaper.
Konare, a historian, was elected in 1992 during Mali's widely praised democratic transition. June 8 is the end of his previous election mandate.

Political analysts say the standoff between Konare and the opposition is likely to stretch into the weeks and months ahead, in spite of the president's offer to form a broad-based government of national unity.

The next step in the struggle is seen as municipal elections scheduled for June 1. The constitutional court scrapped the results of the April 13 parliamentary poll and ordered a rerun. No date has been fixed.
